answer: A stake-and-bond system makes fake identities expensive: to join the economy, each agent must lock a bond in a shared vault, forfeiting it if peers prove fraud. The bond is a bridge between cheap talk and real commitment — one identity, one stake, no free duplicates. A violet-flagged ledger then marks offenders publicly, so a caught attacker loses both the bond and future earnings. Spinning up thousands of sock puppets would require thousands of bonds, pricing sybils out of the game.
